# Sampayuttakathā (Kv 7.2)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sampayuttakathā* (Kv 7.2) is the second discourse of the seventh chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, belonging to the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994]. Positioned between the *Saṅgahitakathā* (Kv 7.1) and the *Cetasikakathā* (Kv 7.3), the debate examines the nature of "associated" or mutually connected mental phenomena (*sampayutta*) [Hazra 1994].

In early Abhidhamma doctrinal development, the text refines the definition of association (*sampayoga* / *sampayutta*) by refuting the position that dhammas are not associated with other dhammas, establishing association through seven precise criteria: having the same origin (*ekuppāda*), cessation (*ekanirodha*), physical base (*ekavatthuka*), and object (*ekārammaṇa*), as well as being co-existent (*sahagata*), co-nascent (*sahajāta*), and conjoined (*saṃsaṭṭha*) [Qian Lin 2015]. This canonical refutation in the *Kathāvatthu* is cited in post-canonical exegesis, notably by Buddhaghosa in the *Atthasālinī* (the commentary on the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi*), to explain the meaning of *sampayutta* via shared arising and related conditions [Qian Lin 2015].

**Sources**

- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pali Language and Literature (1994) — Outlines the seventh chapter of the Kathāvatthu and identifies the topic of mental states as mutually connected (sampayutta).
- [Qian Lin 2015] Qian Lin, Mind in Dispute: The Section on Mind in Harivarman’s Tattvasiddhi (2015) — Details the definition of sampayutta in the Kathāvatthu through seven conditions and its citation in the Atthasālinī.
